nuggets.text: The Tigers' Howard's Rock was a gift sent 'from Death Valley, California, to Death Valley, South Carolina.'
The Tigers first ran past Howard's Rock on Sept. 24, 1966, and beat Virginia 40-35 that day.
Brent Musburger called the Tigers' run down the hill 'The Most Exciting 25 Seconds in College Football.'
Scholarship athletes did much of the early construction work on Memorial Stadium, the Tigers' home since 1942.
Memorial Stadium set a college football loudness record of 133 decibels when the Tigers hosted Boston College in 2007.
After every Tigers home game, fans may come onto the field to sing the alma mater and gather at midfield.
Tigers coach Dabo Swinney's nickname came from his brother Tripp trying to say 'that boy.'
Tigers coach Dabo Swinney joined Alabama as a walk-on wide receiver in 1989.
Tigers coach Dabo Swinney spent 2001 to 2003 selling commercial real estate instead of coaching.
Tigers offensive coordinator Chad Morris never played college football; he earned a math degree at Texas A&M.
